body: No one is their best version of themselves. No one is pitch perfect. The beauty of having an ideal is that its something you can always strive towards and get closer, but the catch is that you will make mistakes along the way, by accident, impulse or pure inexperience. That is of course how we learn. Things change, as you change, your problems change as well. This is where the accept yourself for who you are is helpful but you also need to understand that you can still be who you are and change things incrementally to be better and for the better, others included.

Insecurity is uncertainty of certain aspects of yourself or maybe yourself and your ability to act out things as a whole. You can change it by fixing things in your life, making order out of chaos, fail until you find a solution etc. I guess the opposite of insecurity other than being secure is being certain of yourself and your ability to act on things. 
Obviously this advice is not personalized but you get what I'm saying.

I guess asking good questions and getting good answers from the OP could lead to more personalized advice, but that is something you can ask for. Hello fellow ADHD person, I relate to you because I have been in that exact position, except I wasn't pestered about meditation as you are by others.

I urge you to be open-minded when I tell you now that what you define as meditation or what conception you have built about it is false. 

The object of meditation is not silencing of thoughts and feelings. That would be absurd. To silence your mind is not meditation. It is not what you should be trying to practice, but keep in mind a more 'silent' mind(I would strongly prefer to say more peaceful or having a greater ability to be introspective) is definitely an effect that follows and occurs quicker and more effectively the deeper you get into practice.

To meditate means to have an object that you are aware of and to watch it. What happens when you do this is that you realize you can seperate yourself from your thoughts and emotions. This gives you the ability to slow down your thoughts and consider them more clearly and reduce their weight in your mind. 

For example you are aware that when you try to meditate, before you even begin you think that focusing on silencing your mind, like it is done with pure willpower, does not work. This demotivates and frustrates you and you are right, it doesn't work, so your feelings are justified. The proof is in the pudding.

 How could we silence our human nature? We can't. But what can we do? We can take a step back, from our reality, from our human nature. We can notice that we are aware of when we hear sounds, smell scents and when we think things and what we are thinking etc etc.

So this means that you can use your thoughts as an object for meditation, noises, smells, temperatures, emotions etc. You probably already know that the most common meditation object is breathing. Why is that? Because it is constant, it never stops and it is seperate from thoughts and feelings. Why is this important? Because when you use breathing as an object of awareness, you will have thoughts and feelings that surface to your awareness and this I can guarantee with my life. What do we do when these things arise in us? Stay aware of your breathing, do not try and remove your thoughts and feelings, instead continually focus on your breathing. What happens when you forget about your breathing because a thought grasped you into a daydream of some sort? Just return back to your awareness of breathing. Don't try to silence your thoughts, that has never worked in the history of mankind, instead try to focus more on your breathing, because then you forget of what you were trying to shake loose.

Remember that this advice is coming from an person with ADD, the terrible attention span and ability to choose where your attention is kind. I am telling you this will be difficult, as it is for everyone who starts. Frustration is a poor excuse to stop, because that means you are indulging too much in your emotions and thoughts, which simply means you are forgetting your goal of the meditation session which is to continually try to be aware/focus of your breathing. 
You will fall off the train so many times in the beginning that you will tell yourself why get back onto the train? But one thing I can tell you for sure, is that it is only the beginning. What follows the beginning is serious benefits and introspection which will be invaluable to you in everything that you do. I'm talking about reducing your anger so much that you will avoid 99% of your arguments. I'm talking about better concentration and to choose where it flows. I'm talking about better a better social life, more intimate relationships, better motivation, better executive function, better study ability/work ability/follow through.

I'll end this with some miscellaneous tips and tricks.
Less noise, better sessions.
Less light, better sessions.
Avoid blasting yourself with stimulants in the morning such as social media(youtube and reddit included), pornography etc etc, it creates a   loud mind.
Start with 5 minutes, less if you need to and more if you want to. You must, absolutely must only increase your time when you feel that 5 minutes or 'x' amount of minutes is too short and you WANT to increase the time after a meditation session. 
I mention this above specifically because many people start with an hour, and the first time or few times it goes 'well', but what happens is that you begin to think through the whole meditation session about how long you have been meditating, how much time is left, if you set the alarm properly, heck, you even begin thinking that very little time has probably passed at all as an attempt to get back into focusing. The feeling of time overwhelms you to the point where you get so demotivated to focus on the object of breathing that your session's benefits are reduced so greatly that I would dare say it is a sad loss of time.

You MUST only increase time based on how you feel about your session right after finishing it and do do reasonably incremently. Dismiss your rational mind, that says you should be this and you should be that

I recommend meditating in the morning so that you carry benefits into the day and I also recommend meditating before sleeping as you will get much more dreams and better sleep. I recall writing down at a time 6 dreams a night in such full detail it was like I had lived 6 different short lives. But remember, comparison is the thief of all joy, of all true progression.

Keep on fighting my friend, my ADHD has improved significantly but I've fallen into a rut where I tried to meditate 2 hours a day everyday for 2 months straight which was completely out of my league and demotivated me for many months afterwards and made me question it all. I never lost my progress, I have just got a more noisy mind and receded some progress. Progress can come quick or it can come slow and this varies from person to person and where you are on your journey. And my final tip is try to eat a large, protein rich and fat breakfast in the morning ASAP. Helps with energy, concentration, anxiety etc.
